Answer: B
Reason: The sequence of images shows initial bilateral opacities (Figure 1) progressing to dense consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete radiological resolution (Figures 5a and 5b). This pattern of rapid progression and subsequent clearing is characteristic of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, which can occur in Weil syndrome (severe leptospirosis), distinguishing it from typical bacterial or viral pneumonias that usually have a slower resolution.
